messages.subject: lognornal distribution on semicontinuous models
parts:
I´m running some semicontinuous models for fish distribution using Elias code and would like to know hot to use lognormal distribution on it instead of gamma distribution.

To keep it simple we can use the code from Elia´s spde tutorial because I get the same kinds of errors running it.

So first i tried the code only changing "gamma" to "lognormal", it didn´t work, of course

library(INLA)

data(PRprec)

jday <- 6
z <- (PRprec[,jday]>0) + 0
y <- ifelse(PRprec[,jday]>0, PRprec[,jday], NA)

data(PRprec); dim(PRprec)
data(PRborder); dim(PRborder)


prdomain <- inla.nonconvex.hull(as.matrix(PRprec[,1:2]),
                                -0.03, -0.05, resolution=c(100,100))

(mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(boundary=prdomain, max.edge=c(.45,1), cutoff=0.2))$n

plot(mesh, asp=1, main=''); lines(PRborder, col=3)

spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh, alpha=2)

A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc=as.matrix(PRprec[,1:2]))

stk.z <- inla.stack(tag='est.z',
                    data=list(z=z, ### occurrence for separate model
                              y=cbind(z, NA)), ### z at first column of y
                    A=list(A, 1),
                    effects=list(
                      list(i.z=1:spde$n.spde),
                      list(z.b0=rep(1,length(z)))))

stk.y <- inla.stack(tag='est.y',
                    data=list(r=y, ### rainfall for separate model
                              y=cbind(NA, y)), ### rainfall at second column
                    A=list(A, 1),
                    effects=list(
                      list(i.y=1:spde$n.spde),
                      list(y.b0=rep(1,length(y)))))

res.z <- inla(z ~ 0 + z.b0 + f(i.z, model=spde), family='binomial',
              data=inla.stack.data(stk.z), control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),
              control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.z), compute=TRUE))
res.y <- inla(r ~ 0 + y.b0 + f(i.y, model=spde), family='lognormal',
              data=inla.stack.data(stk.y), control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),
              control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.y), compute=TRUE))

stk.zy <- inla.stack(stk.z, stk.y)


res.zy <- inla(y ~ 0 + z.b0 + y.b0 +
                 f(i.z, model=spde) + f(i.y, copy='i.z', fixed=FALSE),
               family=c('binomial', 'lognormal'),
               data=inla.stack.data(stk.zy), control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),
               control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.zy), compute=TRUE))


res.yz <- inla(y ~ 0 + z.b0 + y.b0 +
                 f(i.y, model=spde) + f(i.z, copy='i.y', fixed=FALSE),
               family=c('binomial', 'lognormal'),
               data=inla.stack.data(stk.zy), control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),
               control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.zy), compute=TRUE))

got the error

Error in inla.create.data.file(y.orig = yy, mf = mf, E = E, scale = scale,  : 
  Responce does not contain variable `truncation'.
In addition: Warning message:
In file.remove(data.dir) :

               family=c('binomial', 'lognormal'),

                 f(i.y, model=spde) + f(i.z, copy='i.y', fixed=FALSE),

               control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.zy), compute=TRUE))

parts:
In the newst testing version, there is 'lognormalsurv' for the survival
lognormal, and 'lognormal' for the regression lognormal. so you can do



n = 300
x = runif(n)
eta = 1+x
y = exp(rnorm(n, mean = eta,  sd = 1))
data = list(y=y, event=rep(1, n), x=x)
formula = inla.surv(y, event) ~ 1 + x
r=inla(formula, family ="lognormalsurv", data=data)
summary(r)

data = data.frame(y, x)
formula = y  ~ 1 + x
r=inla(formula, family ="lognormal", data=data)
summary(r)


and the results should be the same.
